QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_74

question.text: Expected exit INR 150 crore in 5 years, 40% target return (hurdle rate). Under the VC method, the present value (post-money valuation today) is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the VC method as discounting the expected terminal/exit value to present value at the estimated hurdle rate. The VC ownership stake is then based on post-money value and the financing amount. Applying the discount: 150 / (1.40)^5 = 150 / 5.378 ≈ INR 27.9 crore, which is the present value or post-money valuation today (before subtracting any investment amount to derive pre-money). The Trap: INR 15 crore and INR 75 crore use incorrect discount factors. INR 150 crore is the undiscounted exit value and ignores the time-value adjustment that is the core of the VC method. Note: The stem previously labelled this figure "pre-money valuation". The workbook formula produces present value or post-money valuation; pre-money would require subtracting the investment amount. The stem and explanation have been corrected to refer to present value / post-money valuation under the VC method.
